verdict.line: You lose if he lands the W (Umbral Dash... wait) chain-root into a clean 3-hit Q before level 6 while your Riposte is down; you win every extended trade from level 3 onward by parrying his engage tool and punishing with vitals.

brief.thesis: Aatrox's entire lane plan is a single committed engage — W (Infernal Chains) or a Q (Darkin Blade) slash into a full combo — and Fiora's W (Riposte) exists specifically to eat that engage and flip it into a stun on him. If you parry correctly this is one of the safer matchups Fiora has into a bruiser; if you trade autos into him instead of holding the parry, his passive sustain and burst run away with the lane.

theirWindow.when: both E charges up, passive icon lit
theirWindow.what: This is his all-in window — he has the mobility to commit and Deathbringer Stance ready to heal off the trade. Do not extend a trade here; hold Riposte for his W chain or a Q slash instead of autoing.

yourWindow.when: both his E charges are on cooldown
yourWindow.what: He has no dash left to disengage or re-engage. Walk up, Q onto a revealed vital, and commit to a full trade — he cannot punish you back or run.

start.why: The extra sustain and auto damage matter more than the shield version here since you're winning trades with Riposte, not tanking his all-in.

boots.why: His entire kit — Q slashes, W chains, autos, passive-empowered auto — is physical damage; flat armor plus the auto-attack reduction blunts his all-in harder than Mercury's Treads does.

core.why: Gives you the extra burst and movement speed to punish the window right after he burns both E charges.
Lifesteal directly counters his passive Deathbringer Stance sustain in extended trades.
Damage-over-time conversion neutralizes his burst combo and keeps you alive through the all-in window.

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacks through the exact extended trades you're forcing after a successful parry, and the healing amp helps you out-sustain his passive.

summoners.why: Flash covers a misjudged parry window against his engage; Teleport keeps you relevant for the side-lane splits you win from level 9 onward.

playing.title: Bank Riposte for his engage
playing.detail: Never use W to poke or dodge a skillshot minion wave — hold it exclusively for his W chain slam or a Q slash aimed at you. Parrying either stuns him and opens a free full combo.

playing.title: Watch the passive stance icon
playing.detail: A lit sword icon over his head means his next auto heals him significantly. Bait it out with a safe poke before committing to a real trade, or time your Riposte around it.

playing.title: Count his E charges
playing.detail: He regenerates E (Umbral Dash) charges independently; if both are down he is fully committed with no escape. That's your signal to walk up and start a fight, not wait for him to reset.

playing.title: Max Q if you're not being all-inned early
playing.detail: Lunge poke damage and cooldown reduction let you punish his cooldowns between levels 3-5 without needing to parry every trade.

playing.title: Use R to close out extended fights
playing.detail: Grand Challenge reveals all four vitals and stacks healing as you hit them — pop it once you're already committed to a trade he can't escape, not as an opener.

playing.title: Punish a whiffed Q chain
playing.detail: If he misses the second or third slash of Darkin Blade, the full chain resets to base cooldown. That's several seconds where he has no threatening ability up — trade freely.

playing.title: Ward for jungle before his level 6 spike
playing.detail: World Ender turns a even skirmish into a loss; track jungler position before extending trades once he's 6, and only fight it out if you can see the jungler is elsewhere.

brief.patchCaveat: Item and rune names drift patch to patch — verify Trinity Force, Death's Dance, and the Precision tree layout are still current before finalizing build order, but the underlying game plan (bait the all-in, parry the engage tool, out-sustain with lifesteal) has held across many seasons of this matchup.
